title: 30-day beginner DSA plan

focus: CS core intensive (OOP 2d, DBMS 4d, OS 4d, CN 3d)
stretch: hard problems on patterns already learned

LEARN.meaning: First contact with a pattern. Read the full Note-this pipeline (and the linked theory) BEFORE coding, then close it and code from an empty file.

APPLY.meaning: Same pattern, new wording. Attempt cold with the stuck ladder. Pipeline stays covered until you have tried.

TWIST.meaning: The pattern plus one modification. Attempt cold; the brainstorm stage names the modification once you reveal it.

DISGUISE.meaning: The pattern hidden inside a story. Clearing it is the proof that the pattern transfers.

daily_blocks.title: Due re-solves
daily_blocks.note: cold re-solve of problems due at +2/+7/+14 days, oldest first; max 2 per day

daily_blocks.title: Yesterday's must-study siblings
daily_blocks.note: one per problem solved yesterday; read the mini-pipeline, write the pseudocode on paper

daily_blocks.title: Today's 4 problems
daily_blocks.note: paper: analyse -> brainstorm -> algorithm -> pseudocode; then code; then Note-this card

daily_blocks.title: Recognition drill
daily_blocks.note: 5 unseen statements: name the pattern and one-line approach, no code

never_miss_twice: a missed day is allowed; on the next day the floor is mandatory before anything else

cut_order.action: drop optional siblings (they stay browsable, never scheduled)
DISGUISE problem moves to the revision queue with a due date 7 days out
TWIST problem is downgraded to SKIM: reveal the pipeline, write the pseudocode on paper, do not code

carry_over: unfinished LEARN and APPLY problems from past days appear in a capped 'carried over' list (max 4) above today's problems; days never move and the plan is never redrawn

calibration.rule: if the measured median pace over days 1-7 is below 4 problems/day, cut-order step 2 applies permanently to days 8-30. This is the only allowed recalibration.

change_budget: design changes only in the Sunday 20-minute review, at most one per week

stuck_ladder.do: Fill the analysis box on paper and write the dumbest correct (brute force) solution. Most 'stuck' is a skipped brute force.
Read the constraints and turn n into a target complexity. Point at the line of your brute force that does the most repeated work and name WHY it is wasted.
Read the theory section linked on this rung. Reveal only the Analyse stage. Close it and try again.
Reveal the Brainstorm stage (brute -> optimal). Close it, write the algorithm in words and the pseudocode yourself, then code.
Reveal everything (or watch the linked video). Then close every tab and code it from an empty file. Mark it revisit with confidence <= 3 - it comes back as a re-solve.

ai_protocol: Never before the 20 minute mark. The struggle is what encodes it.
Never paste the problem and ask for a solution.
Ask: 'Here is my approach: X. Where does it break?'
Ask: 'What invariant should I be maintaining here?'
Ask: 'I have an O(n^2). What property of the input am I not exploiting?'
After solving: 'Here is my code, review it like a FAANG interviewer.' Most valuable, least used.
Separate session, always. Keeps you from asking earlier and earlier.
Anything that needed a hint is not done, it is scheduled. Set confidence <= 3 and redo it cold in 48 hrs.
